expected.moments: C_m and G_m of the 8 monitored matrices on the 6.4M calibration tokens, every eigenvalue reported; the shares of tr C from position 0 and from the mean reported (RT4). No expected value: inputs to S
expected.stage0_core: the source and the staged file match their filed sha256 and the staged class is the source block with the one patch. Any miss stops

known_range.rule: ww_detector.planted: our path, the staged class and these planted answers equal exactly (float64 latents of exact unit norm). A value at c_max + 0.01 or c_min - 0.01 is not flagged; c_max + 0.0101 and c_min - 0.0101 are. Any difference stops

dW0.rule: F = M keeps no direction (stop otherwise); S is undefined; no window can be flagged

expected.lambda_max: S of dW = u_max e_0^T at h.1.mlp.down_proj reads d lam_max / tr C within the fp64 floor (ww_score.quad_floor: the eigensolver residual plus twice gamma_2d |u|^T |C| |u|, relative to lam). A miss stops
expected.lambda_min: S of dW = u_min e_slot^T reads d lam_min / tr C within the same floor at its site. A miss stops

x2.rule: exactly 8 kept vectors, all at h.1.mlp.down_proj, else stop. Its filed S: S of the exact fp64 dW = W_1,down[:, C] with M's C, written to stage0.json before any other item; the bar is the relative gap of x2's realised S to it

expected.x10: x2 and x10 each within x2's bar of the filed S (known answer, reported)
expected.x10_rate_lean: x10's copy24 flag rate at least x2's (a lean, reported)
expected.parity: on 500 calibration windows and up to 100 rows of each task set, of x2 (ragged: 8 directions in one layer) and of the trigger: the staged class and our path give identical FPR, pass-1 flags, installed ranges and read-only flags. Any difference stops

trigger.gamma: the smallest power of 2 at which the replay flags all 200 build windows along u_min against F's installed ranges; none up to 2^20 stops
trigger.share_T: at least 0.95 of the 1,000 T test windows flagged by F's full pass, else stop
trigger.unchanged: the unchanged test windows at the FPR: the FPR inside the 95% Wilson interval of their flag rate (reported)
trigger.S: the realised S near d lam_min / tr C (reported; the exact check is lambda_min)

expected.gaussian: the mean S of the 20 Gaussian draws within 3 standard errors (of those draws) of 1 (reported)
expected.kept_counts: E62 and panel states keep 20 vectors in every monitored matrix; each sham keeps its item's count per matrix (reported, both)
expected.new_edits: new_few and new_thin near M's floor with their own directions (descriptive: the slots fire on Pile, so calibrating on F takes their firing in)
expected.fpr_reference: Remark 3.1's 2t/n with each state's t after D2, beside each FPR: a reference, not a ceiling or a stop
expected.S: descriptive for every built and trained state, reported against its Haar draws (rank among them) with no band; S_cov and S_G beside

rules.column_rule: redteam-lead 2026-11-23: S earns a column only if (1) x2's S exceeds max(S of new_few, S of new_thin) by more than the Haar spread, the largest (max - min) of the 20 draws of x2, new_few and new_thin; (2) the trigger flags at least 0.95 of its T windows; (3) the dW = 0 control holds (no direction kept, no window flagged). Strict 'more than' on (1); any undefined S or spread fails it. Otherwise S is reported as a related-work negative (ww_score.column_rule)
rules.trained_reading: redteam-lead 2026-11-23: a trained state's (E62, panel) S above all its Haar draws is never read as reuse; it is reported beside S_G as 'at the level the gradient geometry gives' (S <= S_G) or 'above both nulls' (S > S_G); otherwise 'inside or below its Haar null' (a tie with the top draw is inside). Neither is a reuse label (ww_score.trained_reading)
rules.e62_pair: E141's pair rule (experiments/update_svd/run.py pair_rule) on S, copy_s0-2 against lookup_s0-2: separates iff |mean gap| > the larger within-side range (descriptive)
rules.flag_rates: compared only within a task set (spec): an item against its sham and its M floor on the same rows
rules.edge_cases: each rule run on its edge cases in tests/test_weightwatch.py before filing: undefined S, empty and one-element draw pools, ties at the bar, a zero reference, n under 10 (pass 1 empty)

blind_to: the detector sees only inputs that move a hidden state outside the calibration range; anything F already does on Pile is absorbed
both readings see only the output side of o_proj and down_proj, nothing of q, k, v, c_fc or input directions, and only the top 20

S reads low when an update strengthens a direction M rarely writes along, and high when a new mechanism writes along a busy one (an unembedding direction); under s^2 pooling the matrix that moved most dominates
the Haar and Gaussian nulls are isotropic in output direction, so S above them may reflect generic alignment of gradient updates with M's high-variance outputs

amendments.what: Amendment 1: the trigger token T (appendix C4). Was: the lowest id >= 256 in none of the calibration windows and none of the test base windows. Now: T is the rarest id >= token_min (fewest occurrences in the 50,000 calibration windows, ties by lowest id) whose detector row (known_edits.detector at the filed detector_ratio 10 and detector_quantile 0.99, with known_edits.build's gain loop) reaches the ratio, among ids leaving at least 73 of the 1,000 test base windows without T. T's calibration windows are removed from the calibration set (every pass); test windows holding T are dropped; the 0.99 quantile is on Pile held-out positions not holding T. detector_ratio, detector_quantile and trigger_bar are unchanged (run.py Run.trigger_token, Run.detector_row, Run.calib)
amendments.why: with the old rule the first absent id (286) reaches 2.96, under the filed 10, so the trigger row cannot be built; the ratio is kept (lead's decision, 2026-11-23)
amendments.windows_needed_source: ww_score.windows_needed(trigger_bar 0.95): the fewest windows whose 95% Wilson interval (ww_score.wilson, the interval the trigger read already uses) with every window flagged lies at or above 0.95, n / (n + 1.96^2) >= 0.95
amendments.T_source: CPU dry run 2026-11-23 (run.py's own path, Run.trigger_token): T 975, absent from the calibration windows, in 1 of the 1,000 test base windows (999 kept), detector ratio 10.562 (whitened ridge 0.01; filed direction 6.81), gain 1, the 11th id tried; the 10 lower absent ids read 2.90-3.01. The GPU run re-chooses by the same rule
amendments.sweep_source: results/trigger_sweep*.json (experiments/weightwatch/trigger_sweep.py, cpu-run 2026-11-23): known_edits.detector's four limits for each id, absent ids by id then the 500 rarest present ids. At filing: 502 of the absent ids read, 210 reach 10 (top: 3 infinite, i.e. no Pile position above zero along the row, then 128.5, 110.0); 421 present ids read, 264 reach 10. The sweep's fast path matches the run's path on T 975 (10.5624 both) and on T 12924 (12.4254 both)

card_spread_proxy: proxy for the card: for a random unit u, sd(a) = sqrt(2 (d sum lam^2 / (sum lam)^2 - 1) / (d + 2)); at an assumed participation ratio of 20 for C (d / PR = 38.4) that is 0.31 per vector, and 0.11 for S pooled over 8 equal-weight vectors (x2's count). Arithmetic on an assumed spectrum, not a measurement: stage 0 measures the Haar spread itself
